description: 7 piezo sensors, one hit event per struck note (no sustain/duration, no breath, no check-button convention -- the hit itself is the check, per project doc claude/controller_hid_protocol.md). Pad numbering/names below (1-7) are AUTHORITATIVE, matching the physical build's HID report layout exactly (button N = pad N, no offset, since drum-kit has no separate check bit): 1=Crash, 2=Snare, 3=High Tom, 4=Kick, 5=Mid Tom, 6=Floor Tom, 7=Ride -- keep this file and docs/beatmap_schema.md's drum pad table in sync if either changes. 2026-08-22: this replaces the earlier placeholder set (1=Kick, 2=Snare, 3=Hi-Hat, 4=High Tom, 5=Floor Tom, 6=Crash, 7=Ride), decided against the actual built controller's firmware (drumkit_control_HID.ino) once the physical 7-piezo layout was finalized -- that kit has no hi-hat pad, so Mid Tom takes its place, and the numbering now follows the controller's physical left-to-right wiring order instead of the earlier placeholder order. The list order below is NOT the same as pad-number order -- it's sorted by approximate perceptual pitch (kick lowest ... crash/ride highest), which is what the converter's piano-mode bass-clef bucketing and band-mode fallback bucketing walk across low-to-high; each entry still carries its correct authoritative 'index'/'name'. Band mode (a real drum/percussion MusicXML or MIDI part) is NOT YET matching by percussion instrument name -- it currently falls back to the same pitch-bucketing as piano mode. That's a known gap, worth revisiting once there's an actual drum-kit part to test against. band_mode_name_map below is prepared for that future work but isn't consulted by convert.py/convert_midi.py yet -- note GM MIDI's own hi-hat-heavy percussion convention doesn't map cleanly onto this kit's hi-hat-less pad set, so GM hi-hat hits will need to be redirected to another pad (most likely Ride) once that mapping is implemented.
